title: Silver Era Aesthetics Program (Steve Reeves Physique Workout)
summary: NH presents a free Silver Era full-body program inspired by Steve Reeves, with an intermediate version (3 sessions/week, Mon-Wed-Fri) and an advanced version (4 sessions, every other day). It emphasizes the V-taper (lats, shoulders), core and arms, uses supersets ordered by a pyramid of priority, and auto-regulated ab training.
claims: Steve Reeves is the most aesthetic natural bodybuilder in history; he started training at 13 and built his physique over years
The Silver Era physique is built on the V-taper: focus on shoulders and lats, plus a well-developed core and arms
Reeves' proportion rules: upper arms should match calves, and arms bigger than the neck mean something is wrong; NH follows these loosely
Full body is the hardest split to program because it demands good recovery and frequency management
This program is too much for novices; they should start with his Greek Statue program as a stepping stone
Auto-regulated abs (intermediate): 80-200 reps per week over 8-10 isolation sets, max 4 sets per day, 10-20 reps per set
Place ab sets after lower-body compounds, never before, so you do not pre-fatigue the core needed to stay rigid in heavy squats
Best Silver Era core exercises: weighted decline sit-ups, weighted leg raises, hanging knee raises, V-sit ups, windshield wipers
Pyramid of priority: open each day with the most strenuous, most important exercise; if short on time, skip the bottom sets, never the top
All pairings in the program are double sets (supersets); the last exercise in a tri-set is always the least important and can be cut
A full-body split of only compounds is garbage, and training every muscle equally every session is mostly garbage too; each day needs different emphases for recovery
The Silver Era did not want to load the hips much or chase big glutes; hamstrings were not a priority, so posterior chain work is optional
Silver Era bodybuilders barely trained the neck; the program includes only 4 sets of neck curls per week
Heavy pullover sets with low reps lead to cheating and shallow ROM; keep pullovers at 8-12 reps; pullover injuries mostly happen at the shoulder
Guillotine press is a risky Silver Era specialty lift due to internal rotation; keep it at 10-15 reps or use rings
Wide-grip pull-ups should use a false grip or fat grip so you palm the bar; with the week's back volume they need no added weight
Full body 3x/week accumulates fatigue to peak on Friday, then the weekend flushes it out and keeps your hunger to train
Intermediates with poor work capacity can drop the last line of each day and add it back as capacity builds
Intermediate = 3 sessions/week, 12/month, 140-150/year; advanced = every other day, 4 sessions/week, 15/month, 180/year, about 30 extra sessions (three months) a year
Advanced abs: 100-240 reps per week over 10-12 isolation sets
On the advanced version, taking an occasional extra day off is fine but if it becomes regular you are back on the intermediate program
More work is not always better, but more work done intelligently with enough recovery is
Snatch-grip shrugs are incredible for the yoke and worth trying
A modern natural full-body trainee (El Zoviak) proves a Silver Era physique is achievable naturally
exercises: Dellinger squat = front squat heels elevated (Gironda)
DB/machine shoulder press or face pull
Pelican cable curl / fat-grip DB preacher curl
low intensity; consider recovery for heavy squats 2 days later
